Subject: MedCo pilot readiness: buying roles, procurement checklist & SLA exception request

Hi Jane — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick internal+external recap and clear asks so we keep momentum for the pilot kickoff in mid-Dec.

1) Stakeholders & decision roles (as discussed)
- Economic buyer: Mark Eldridge (CFO) — expects clear pilot ROI and TCO projections
- Procurement lead: procurement@medcohealth.com (SOC/procurement packet + contract routing)
- Security reviewer: Mark S. (security@medcohealth.com) — will need SOC2 evidence and data flow diagrams
- Product/POC owner: Jane Doe — will run day-to-day pilot ops

2) Decision criteria Jane called out
- Successful integration with their data pipeline (S3 -> private VPC connector)
- Latency < 400ms p95 for targeted inference flows
- Proof of no persistent PHI storage and audit logs available for 30 days
- Reasonable cost per request vs current baseline

3) Procurement asks & exception requests (action items we need internal clearance for)
- SLA exception: MedCo is requesting an SLA addendum that guarantees higher availability and RTO for pilot traffic during business hours. They want a one-off SLA variance (short window) while we test.
- Commercial: 15% pilot discount + $25k credit to offset integration engineering time
- Security: provide SOC2 snapshot + network diagram (attached) and confirm audit logging retention policy

Attachments: medco_sow_draft.pdf, medco_security_snapshot_2026-10.zip

Internal asks (cc'd)
- Rishi: can you approve the 15% pilot discount + $25k credit for this deal as a one-time pilot concession?
- Laura: I need a procurement checklist we can send to procurement@medcohealth.com and a recommended clause for a limited SLA exception.
- Marissa: please prepare a short stakeholder map we can include in the HubSpot deal.

External ask (Jane)
- Please share the primary procurement intake form (if you have one) and confirm the desired pilot start (target week of Dec 13).

I'll stand by for internal approvals — if we can lock the exceptions this week we can route DocuSign next Monday and start integration the week after.

Best,
Ben

Folks — forwarding Jane's reply (below) and asking for quick next steps. We need to put a one-page exception request together for procurement and a short justification for the SLA variance. Draft below that I plan to send to procurement once I get approvals.

--- draft exception request (business justification) ---
Summary: MedCo Health is requesting a limited SLA exception during a 90-day pilot to accelerate evaluation and integration. In exchange we will provide a 15% pilot discount and $25k engineering credit. The pilot focuses on a single non-PHI dataset and will be run inside a private VPC connector with no persistent storage beyond 30-day audit logs.
Business reason: The pilot is with a high-value prospect (CFO-led) with expected annualized ARR if successful of >$1.2M. Accelerating the pilot reduces time-to-value and increases probability of expansion into dedicated capacity.
Security mitigations: SOC2 evidence attached; network diagram; strict IAM roles and audit logging; egress limited to whitelisted IPs.
Requested approvals: commercial discount (15% + $25k credit), SLA variance for pilot window, and procurement acceptance of the limited clause.
--- end draft ---

Action items:
- Rishi: please confirm commercial approval and any cap on credit.
- Laura: I need the exact procurement checklist and suggested clause language for the SLA variance. If legal needs to review, can you indicate estimated turnaround and owners?
- Marissa: create the one-pager stakeholder map and add to HubSpot (linked).

I want to send to procurement by EOD today if approvals are green.

Thanks,
Ben

Ben/Rishi/Marissa — acknowledged. I'm looping procurement@medcohealth.com as requested so they have the inbound thread for records. Below is the procurement/contract playbook and the minimal SLA exception language I recommend for a pilot. I'll mark legal and security review owners.

Procurement checklist (what we will provide)
- Signed SOW (attached) and pilot scope clarified
- Formal exception request doc (one paragraph business justification + approved concession language)
- SOC2 snapshot + network diagram (Ben attached)
- Point of contact for invoices and billing
- Insurance & standard vendor paperwork (W-9, vendor form — we have templates if they need)

Minimal SLA exception clause (recommended wording)
"For the duration of the Pilot (90 days starting on the Effective Date), the Parties agree to a limited SLA arrangement as set forth in Appendix X. This limited SLA shall apply only to Pilot traffic and does not constitute a permanent amendment to the Agreement. Redwood's obligation under the limited SLA is contingent upon receipt of Security's written sign-off that required controls (SOC2 evidence, network diagram, audit logging) are in place. Any permanent SLA amendment will require separate negotiation and legal approval."

Owners and estimated turnaround
- Procurement review (Laura Bennett) — 2 business days after receipt of exception doc and SOW
- Legal review (contracts@redwood.com; cc Rishi) — 3 business days if no material changes to standard terms
- Security sign-off (security@redwood.com) — 48 hours after SOC2 and network diagram reviewed

If procurement@medcohealth.com confirms receipt, I'll issue a short exception packet and route to contracts for signature. Ben — please update HubSpot RDW-9842 and attach the finalized one-pager. Marissa — can you have the stakeholder map in HubSpot by EOD?
